::: {.gallery-demo-notes}
### What is being estimated?

`npcdist()` estimates the conditional distribution with `year` treated as an
ordered factor. `npqreg()` inverts it:
$Q_\tau(\mathrm{year}) = F^{-1}(\tau \mid \mathrm{year})$. At `tau = 0.5`,
this is the conditional median. Reusing `Fhat$bws` avoids another bandwidth
search. The grey traces show the same quantile at *F* = `tau` and on the floor
at *F* = 0; the 3D rug marks the observed support. The opening angle emphasizes
the floor projection, while rotation reveals its relationship to the surface.
The panel combines a historical [SVIMEZ reconstruction](https://datimezzogiorno.svimez.it/en/the-data/svimez-statistics-1861-2011/)
with modern [ARDECO regional data](https://territorial.ec.europa.eu/ardeco/viewer/SOVGDP).

The expanded data are included with `np` 0.80-3. Download the
[R script](www/np_npRmpi/np_italy_conditional_distribution_rgl.R), or expand
the example below.
:::

::: {.gallery-code-disclosure}
::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Reproduce and adapt this figure

```r
## Load the package and updated Italian regional panel
library(np)
# This example requires the suggested rgl package: install.packages("rgl")
data("Italy_Updated")
# gdp is real GDP per capita in thousands of 2020 euros.

## Estimate F(gdp | year), then face its floor projection toward the viewer
Fhat <- npcdist(gdp ~ year, data = Italy_Updated)
widget <- plot(Fhat, renderer = "rgl", zlab = "F(gdp|year)",
  theta = 300, phi = 10, data.rug = TRUE)

## Reuse its bandwidths to estimate a conditional quantile without a new search
tau <- 0.5 # Use 0.25 for the conditional first quartile, and so forth.
Qhat <- npqreg(bws = Fhat$bws, tau = tau, data = Italy_Updated)
# Optional: plot(Qhat) draws the conditional quantile.
# plot(Qhat, gradients = TRUE) draws its marginal effect, \Delta Q / \Delta year.
year_grid <- data.frame(
  year = ordered(levels(Italy_Updated$year),
    levels = levels(Italy_Updated$year)))
year_num <- as.numeric(as.character(year_grid$year))
cond_quantile <- drop(predict(Qhat, newdata = year_grid))

## Trace the selected quantile at F = tau and project it onto the floor
rgl::plot3d(widget)
rgl::lines3d(year_num, cond_quantile, 0, color = "grey45", lwd = 1.5)
rgl::lines3d(year_num, cond_quantile, tau, color = "grey45", lwd = 1)
rgl::rglwidget()
```
:::
:::

::: {.gallery-code-disclosure}
::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Compare cell-based and joint estimates

The first panel below estimates each year's CDF separately, including a
separate GDP bandwidth. The second remains cell-based by fixing the ordered
year bandwidth at `lambda = 0`, but selects one common GDP bandwidth across
years. The final `npcdist()` fit also borrows strength across the ordered year
axis. Comparing all three separates the effect of a common bandwidth from the
additional smoothing supplied by neighboring years. With only 20 regions per
year, the joint fit produces a markedly steadier year-to-year CDF and median
path than independent annual fits in this example.

```r
## Load the data and define a common evaluation grid
# This comparison requires the suggested rgl package: install.packages("rgl")
options(rgl.useNULL = TRUE) # Avoid native OpenGL warnings for HTML widgets.
library(np)
data("Italy_Updated")
set.seed(20261114)

years <- levels(Italy_Updated$year)
year_num <- as.numeric(years)
gdp_grid <- seq(0, ceiling(max(Italy_Updated$gdp) * 1.05),
  length.out = 121)
tau <- 0.5

## Estimate each year's CDF and median using its own selected bandwidth
annual_fit <- lapply(years, function(yr) {
  annual_data <- droplevels(
    Italy_Updated[Italy_Updated$year == yr, , drop = FALSE])
  bw <- npudistbw(~gdp, data = annual_data)
  Fhat <- npudist(bws = bw, newdata = data.frame(gdp = gdp_grid))
  list(
    cdf = fitted(Fhat),
    quantile = npquantile(annual_data$gdp, tau = tau, bws = bw))
})
cdf_separate <- do.call(rbind, lapply(annual_fit, `[[`, "cdf"))
quantile_separate <- vapply(annual_fit,
  function(fit) unname(fit$quantile), numeric(1))

## Assemble a common year-by-GDP evaluation grid
eval_grid <- expand.grid(
  year = ordered(years, levels = years),
  gdp = gdp_grid,
  KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE)
year_grid <- data.frame(year = ordered(years, levels = years))

evaluate_conditional_fit <- function(bws) {
  Fhat <- npcdist(bws = bws, newdata = eval_grid)
  Qhat <- npqreg(bws = bws, tau = tau, data = Italy_Updated)
  list(
    cdf = matrix(fitted(Fhat), nrow = length(years)),
    quantile = drop(predict(Qhat, newdata = year_grid)))
}

## Select one GDP bandwidth while retaining cell-based year estimates
bw_common <- npcdistbw(gdp ~ year, data = Italy_Updated,
  lbd.dir = 0, hbd.dir = 0, dfac.dir = 0, initd.dir = 0,
  lbd.init = 0, hbd.init = 0, dfac.init = 0)
stopifnot(as.numeric(bw_common$xbw) == 0)
common_fit <- evaluate_conditional_fit(bw_common)

## Jointly select the GDP and ordered-year bandwidths
joint_model <- npcdist(gdp ~ year, data = Italy_Updated)
joint_fit <- evaluate_conditional_fit(joint_model$bws)

## Use np's viridis surface palette and its small RGL boundary clearance
palette <- grDevices::hcl.colors(1000, palette = "viridis")
cdf_limits <- grDevices::extendrange(c(0, 1), f = 0.001)
surface_colors <- function(cdf) {
  index <- 1 + floor(999 * pmax(0, pmin(1, cdf)))
  matrix(palette[index], nrow = nrow(cdf), ncol = ncol(cdf))
}

draw_panel <- function(cdf, quantile, title) {
  rgl::persp3d(year_num, gdp_grid, cdf, zlim = cdf_limits,
    xlab = "year",
    ylab = "real GDP per capita (thousands of 2020 euros)",
    zlab = "F(gdp|year)", main = title, ticktype = "detailed",
    color = surface_colors(cdf), alpha = 0.6, back = "lines",
    border = palette[32], lit = FALSE)
  rgl::points3d(as.numeric(as.character(Italy_Updated$year)),
    Italy_Updated$gdp, 0, color = "grey55", alpha = 0.35, size = 2)
  rgl::lines3d(year_num, quantile, tau, color = "grey30", lwd = 1)
  rgl::lines3d(year_num, quantile, 0, color = "grey30", lwd = 1.5)
  rgl::grid3d(c("x", "y+", "z"), col = "grey", lwd = 1)
  rgl::view3d(theta = 300, phi = 10, fov = 55)
}

## Draw synchronized panels that rotate and zoom together
rgl::open3d(useNULL = TRUE, silent = TRUE)
rgl::mfrow3d(1, 3, sharedMouse = TRUE)
draw_panel(cdf_separate, quantile_separate,
  "Separate bandwidth per year")
rgl::next3d()
draw_panel(common_fit$cdf, common_fit$quantile,
  "Common GDP bandwidth, lambda = 0")
rgl::next3d()
draw_panel(joint_fit$cdf, joint_fit$quantile,
  "Ordered-year-smoothed npcdist")
rgl::rglwidget(width = 2100, height = 720)
```
:::
:::

## Current package status

The examples use `np` `{{< var current-releases.np.version >}}`, `npRmpi`
`{{< var current-releases.npRmpi.version >}}` (published
{{< var current-releases.npRmpi.published >}}), and `crs`
`{{< var current-releases.crs.version >}}` (published
{{< var current-releases.crs.published >}}).

The [0.80-3 migration note](faq.qmd#what-should-i-check-when-moving-to-080-3)
summarizes the argument changes most likely to affect older code.

## Current Capabilities

- [0.80-3 update and migration notes](runtime_and_scaling.qmd): `np` and `npRmpi` add `npindextest()` and `nppltest()`, standardize bootstrap reporting across ten public tests, bundle `Italy_Updated`, improve numerical and search edge cases, and reduce repeated data movement in `npRmpi`.
- [Spline updates](crs.qmd): `crs` `0.15-46` retains the common named plotting controls and `crshat()` operator workflow, adds formula/data and S3 support for instrumental spline regression, and provides the observed NOMAD interface used for responsive progress in downstream degree searches.
- [Local polynomial workflows](np_npRmpi.qmd): `np` and `npRmpi` support local polynomial capability across the conditional family, with joint selection of polynomial degrees and bandwidths for mixed data, gradient support throughout the conditional estimators, and derivative estimation of arbitrarily high order, limited only by the selected polynomial degree whether set manually or chosen automatically for the underlying smoothness class.
- [Boundary-aware density estimation](boundary_aware_density.qmd): unconditional and conditional density workflows support known two-sided or one-sided bounds and practical unknown-bound proxies, with a worked example showing what changes in finite- and unbounded-support settings.
- [Location-scale quantile regression](density_distribution_quantiles.qmd): `nplsqreg` and `nplsqregbw` provide a first-class location-scale quantile workflow with formula and bandwidth-object routes, scalar or vector `tau`, stored-quantile selection through `predict(..., tau = ...)`, residuals, summaries, plots, and the same NOMAD-enabled local-polynomial degree-and-bandwidth search style where supported.
- [Conditional quantile regression](density_distribution_quantiles.qmd): `npqreg` provides a direct formula interface, automatic `npcdistbw()` bandwidth selection when `bws` is omitted, vector `tau` support, `plot(..., tau = ...)` reuse of existing bandwidths, conditional-quantile gradients and standard errors, and `nomad = "auto"` pass-through for local-polynomial degree-and-bandwidth search.
- [Conditional mode classification](classification_modes.qmd): `npconmode` is a first-class high-level estimator, with direct formula/data/newdata workflows, automatic `npcdensbw()` bandwidth selection when `bws` is omitted, conditional-density search controls including `nomad = "auto"`, mirrored degree/search metadata in returned objects and summaries, properized fitted class probabilities for non-local-constant routes before selecting the modal outcome, and level-specific class-probability effects.
- [Copula estimation](density_distribution_quantiles.qmd): `npcopula` is a first-class high-level estimator with a direct formula interface, automatic `npudistbw()` or `npudensbw()` selection when `bws` is omitted, automatic two-dimensional probability-grid construction for the default grid route, and easy reuse of the selected bandwidth object when you want a custom `u` grid or copula-density target.
- [Hat-matrix and operator helpers](semiparametric_models.qmd): `npreghat`, `npindexhat`, `npplreghat`, and `npscoefhat` provide one-call operator routes that simplify constrained nonparametric and semiparametric estimation by replacing much of the manual hat-matrix construction and solve-based setup, while `npudenshat`, `npudisthat`, `npcdenshat`, and `npcdisthat` extend the same streamlined operator style to the density/distribution family.
- [Variability bounds on plots](plotting_and_intervals.qmd): pointwise, Bonferroni, and simultaneous bounds share the plotting surface across supported regression, density/distribution, quantile, class-probability, and copula targets, and `band = "all"` presents all three together.
- [Interactive plotting surfaces](plotting_and_intervals.qmd): `renderer = "rgl"` supports interactive 3D rotation/zoom when `rgl` is installed, while `data.rug` and `data.overlay` control rugs and observed-data overlays on supported routes.
- [MPI operational routes](mpi_large_data.qmd): `npRmpi` session and attach routes let users work directly with `np`-style code, while the profile route remains available when needed.

## Notes

- Search should help if you know the function name but not where it lives.
- [Quickstarts](quickstarts.qmd) is the shortest route to a small runnable script.
- The reference page groups functions by task rather than repeating a long handwritten index.
- Additional resources, including books and papers, are collected on [Books, Papers, and Citation](books_papers.qmd).

Feedback is welcome. My academic page is [experts.mcmaster.ca/display/racinej](https://experts.mcmaster.ca/display/racinej), and additional materials remain available at [jeffreyracine.github.io/research](https://jeffreyracine.github.io/research).
